run.question:
The checkout-service in production-eu-west-2 is throwing 500s. Please look at
app-264-prod-logs and find the root cause.

report.summary: I could not find any evidence for checkout-service in production-eu-west-2. The requested index app-264-prod-logs is the only index on this Elasticsearch source and holds 3 documents in total for the authorized window (2026-11-21T08:55:04Z to 2026-11-22T08:55:04Z), and every one of them carries cluster=staging-eu-west-2, environment=staging, region=eu-west-2 — not production-eu-west-2. Two of those staging-labelled documents are ERROR lines from service checkout-service: "POST /api/checkout returned 500: integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired" (2026-11-22T07:54:56Z) and "Smoke test failed: deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress" (2026-11-22T06:54:56Z); the third is a payment-service WARN about the staging stripe mock. Those are records of a different cluster/environment label, so I do not name anything from them as the root cause of the production-eu-west-2 incident. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable for the whole run (every query returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no metric or trace evidence about checkout 500s in any cluster could be read. On the only Kubernetes cluster I can read (staging-eu-west-2, per my access scope) the otel-demo checkout deployment and pod are up and its current logs show only successful PlaceOrder/payment/email messages between 08:16:39Z and 08:55:01Z; the flagd-config fault flags there are all defaultVariant off. No root cause can be asserted for production-eu-west-2 from the available data.

claims.text: app-264-prod-logs is the only index on this Elasticsearch source; it maps fields cluster, environment, level, message, region, service and date field timestamp, and contains 3 documents.

Querying app-264-prod-logs over the whole authorized window returned total=3 (relation eq) with documents_shown=3, and all three documents carry cluster=staging-eu-west-2, environment=staging, region=eu-west-2; none of the returned documents carries cluster or environment production-eu-west-2 / production.

Among those documents, service checkout-service logged level ERROR at 2026-11-22T07:54:56Z with message "POST /api/checkout returned 500: integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired" and level ERROR at 2026-11-22T06:54:56Z with message "Smoke test failed: deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress", both with cluster=staging-eu-west-2 and environment=staging.
The third document is a level WARN from service payment-service at 2026-11-22T08:24:56Z: "Using mock provider for staging (stripe-mock)", cluster=staging-eu-west-2, environment=staging.

The hypothesis that app-264-prod-logs contains the production-eu-west-2 checkout-service 500 logs is contradicted by the data: the index's complete set of documents in the window (total 3) is labelled cluster=staging-eu-west-2 and environment=staging, so those checkout ERROR lines belong to a staging-labelled environment and cannot be attributed to production-eu-west-2.

On the Kubernetes cluster I can read (staging-eu-west-2 per my access scope) all 21 otel-demo deployments report readyReplicas=1, availableReplicas=1, updatedReplicas=1, and the checkout deployment image is ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout (no v2.3.4 image present).

The staging-eu-west-2 checkout pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n is Running and ready (restartCount 2) and its current-container logs, 200 newest of 254 lines spanning 2026-11-22T08:16:39.595Z to 2026-11-22T08:55:01.193Z, contain only info-level messages: "[PlaceOrder] user_id=...", "payment went through (transaction_id: ...)" and "order confirmation email sent to ..."; no error or failed-checkout line appears among the returned lines.

In the staging-eu-west-2 payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d, filtering its 175 log lines (2026-11-22T08:04:22Z to 08:55:01Z) with 'err|error|fail|exception|panic|mock|stripe' returned exactly 1 line, "MetadataLookupWarning: ... Invalid response from metadata service: incorrect Metadata-Flavor header" at 2026-11-22T08:04:24Z; 174 lines were removed by that filter, so no stripe-mock line appears in these pod logs.

The otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) declares 11 fault flags — productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad — and every one has defaultVariant "off"; state is ENABLED but no injected fault is switched on in this cluster.

Events in the staging-eu-west-2 cluster include Pod-level probe failures and a container backoff confined to kube-state-metrics-7cbf5b996-df4sz (Unhealthy liveness/readiness 08:04:30–08:04:50Z, Killing 08:04:50Z), otel-collector-789c64b9bf-tl55c (Unhealthy readiness 08:04:22Z) and prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn (Unhealthy 08:04:23–08:05:10Z, BackOff restarting failed container nginx 08:04:27–08:04:44Z); no event in the window involves a checkout pod.

Two Endpoints events exist in the staging-eu-west-2 cluster, both FailedToCreateEndpoint and both for objects in different namespaces/app labels than otel-demo: "Failed to create endpoint for service app-217/postgres: endpoints \"postgres\" already exists" (2026-11-21T09:05:28Z) and the same message for service app-223/sqlserver (2026-11-21T09:21:49Z).

If the person reporting "checkout-service in production-eu-west-2" is actually looking at the environment recorded in app-264-prod-logs, the failing operation is checkout's POST /api/checkout returning 500 and the log line states its cause as an expired integration-test Stripe key (stripe-test-key) in that staging-labelled environment; this remains a hypothesis because no production-labelled data source exists in this run and the staging checkout pod itself logs only completed payments.

The Prometheus and Jaeger read paths being unavailable to this Run may be related to the staging-eu-west-2 otel-demo probe failures and nginx container BackOff seen on prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn (6 restarts, last termination reason Error exit 1) and the otel-collector readiness failure around 08:04–08:05Z; this is unproven because the proxy pod currently reports Running/ready and no metric or trace query could be executed to confirm either link.

Have the requester confirm the log index, cluster label and environment that actually serve production-eu-west-2 checkout traffic, since the named index app-264-prod-logs holds only staging-eu-west-2 / environment=staging documents.

Restore Prometheus (via prometheus-readonly-proxy) and Jaeger read access so checkout 5xx rate and error spans can be measured; then compare checkout 500 rate in the production environment against a baseline window before judging a trend.

gaps: No data labelled production-eu-west-2 exists in any source I could read: the only Elasticsearch index (app-264-prod-logs) holds 3 documents, all cluster=staging-eu-west-2 / environment=staging, and Kubernetes access in this Run is only to staging-eu-west-2.

Prometheus was unreachable for the entire run: get_metric_names {__name__=~"traces_.*"}, get_all_labels {service_name="checkout"}, get_label_values service_name, and execute_prometheus_instant_query 'up' all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no checkout error-rate, ERROR-series or latency evidence was obtainable (these resulted in no data, not zero).

Jaeger was unreachable for the entire run: traces_list_services, traces_search service=checkout and traces_search_by_tags all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span or error-tag evidence for checkout exists in this Run.

Whether the reported 500s are currently occurring in production-eu-west-2 is unknown: no production logs, metrics or traces were available; the two checkout ERROR documents found are labelled staging-eu-west-2 and describe an expired integration-test fixture and a smoke-test rollback message.

The Stripe credential value named in the staging error text cannot be inspected (secrets are not readable), so whether an expired key is actually in use anywhere serving production traffic could not be verified.
The change_history integration is not available, so no deployment or configuration change record for production-eu-west-2 could be checked.
Why the Prometheus and Jaeger tools returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE is unknown; the staging prometheus-readonly-proxy BackOff events are a possible but unconfirmed link.

Pods report restartCount values with lastState reason Unknown/exit code 255 across the otel-demo namespace (e.g. checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n restartCount 2, previous container stream read returned 0 lines), so no previous-instance crash reason could be read for the checkout container.
next_steps: Identify the actual production-eu-west-2 log/metric/trace backend (index name, cluster label) and re-run this investigation against it.
Once Prometheus is reachable, measure checkout 5xx rate and p95 latency for the incident window versus an equivalent pre-incident baseline.

In the environment that serves production checkout traffic, verify the payment/Stripe credential validity (the staging record names an expired integration-test key) and check whether payment-service is configured to use a mock provider there.

Confirm whether a deploy or rollback (the staging record mentions deploy-v2.3.4 rollback) occurred on the production checkout workload, using a change-history source that is not available in this Run.
